root_cause.statement: Structured-output requests to inkling-small die with a 500 because the first token(s) generated immediately after the reasoning-end marker escape the xgrammar bitmask and are then fed fatally to grammar.accept_tokens. inkling has a reasoning parser, so structured_output_manager.should_fill_bitmask gates the grammar bitmask on reasoning_ended (backend __init__.py:361-379). reasoning_ended is only flipped True later, inside update_from_output via should_advance (__init__.py:381-439). Under async scheduling (and/or MTP speculative decoding, which inkling ships as inkling_mtp), the next step's bitmask is computed before reasoning_ended is persisted, so the token right after the reasoning-end marker (<|content_text|> id 200004 / <|content_model_end_sampling|> id 200006, per InklingParser.is_reasoning_end) is sampled with NO grammar constraint. The model then emits a special/control token the JSON grammar never permits -- here <|begin_of_text|> id 200028 -- and the scheduler, after trim_reasoning_for_advance strips the reasoning prefix, calls grammar.accept_tokens([200028,...]), which returns False, and the scheduler treats that as fatal (RequestStatus.FINISHED_ERROR) -> 'grammar rejected tokens [200028]' -> 500.
root_cause.mechanism: 1) inkling is a reasoner-backed model, so during reasoning should_fill_bitmask returns False and no bitmask is applied; the model samples freely. 2) reasoning_ended is detected/persisted only in the output path (should_advance in update_from_output), which runs AFTER the next step has already been scheduled (async) or after multiple draft positions were already sampled unconstrained within one window (MTP spec decode). 3) Consequently the first post-marker token is sampled without the grammar bitmask (in non-spec async, grammar_bitmask only fills the bonus-token mask with should_fill_bitmask()==False; in spec decode, the detect_reasoning_end loop only flips apply_bitmask True AFTER the marker and its own accept_tokens deliberately tolerates rejection of these pre-bitmask drafts, __init__.py:303-331). 4) The target accepts that unconstrained token into generated_token_ids (=new_token_ids). 5) At scheduler.py:1828-1856 should_advance fires (reasoning ended this step), trim_reasoning_for_advance drops through the reasoning-end marker, and the surviving suffix [200028, ...] is handed to XgrammarGrammar.accept_tokens (backend_xgrammar.py:152-171), which rejects any token invalid at the current JSON state. 6) Unlike the bitmask-fill path, the scheduler output path has NO tolerance: a False return sets FINISHED_ERROR/resumable=False and hard-terminates. That asymmetry -- tolerant in grammar_bitmask, fatal in update_from_output -- is the defect. That 200028 is <|begin_of_text|> (a stray in-vocab special token, NOT one of inkling's block/content markers and NOT the model's stop token 200006) rules out a simple trim off-by-one on a known marker and confirms an unconstrained sample leaked past the grammar.

keystone_facts.fact: Token id 200028 for thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small-NVFP4 is the special token <|begin_of_text|> (added_tokens_decoder["200028"].content = '<|begin_of_text|>', special=true). It is a control/BOS-style special token, NOT one of inkling's content/block markers and NOT the stop token; a JSON-schema grammar never allows it, and xgrammar masks it under constraint.

keystone_facts.fact: eos_token_id = 200006 = <|content_model_end_sampling|>. So the grammar's allowed terminal/stop token is 200006, not 200028; 200028 is unrelated to normal grammar termination.

keystone_facts.fact: vocab_size = 201024, which is > 200028. The rejected token is therefore a normal in-vocab special token, NOT a token above the compiled vocab_size / outside the bitmask's index range. The failure is a bitmask-application timing race, not an out-of-bounds/vocab-size mismatch.
keystone_facts.source: HuggingFace thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small-NVFP4 config.json (vocab_size); backend uses model_config.get_vocab_size() at __init__.py:130 for the xgrammar bitmask width

proposed_fix.summary: Make the reasoning->grammar handoff not lose grammar constraint and not fatally terminate on tokens that were sampled before the bitmask could apply. Two complementary changes: (A) close the timing race so the first post-reasoning token is actually bitmask-constrained, and (B) make the scheduler's boundary acceptance tolerant (validate-and-rollback) instead of a hard request error, mirroring the tolerance already present in grammar_bitmask.

changes.what: At the should_advance/trim/accept_tokens block (~1828-1856): when reasoning ended in THIS step, do not treat an accept_tokens rejection as fatal. Accept the valid prefix (like XgrammarGrammar.validate_tokens) and treat the first invalid post-marker token and everything after it as spec-rejected: roll back num_computed_tokens/num_output_placeholders and truncate new_token_ids for those positions so they are re-sampled next step WITH the grammar bitmask, instead of setting FINISHED_ERROR. Reserve FINISHED_ERROR for rejections that occur strictly after reasoning has already ended in a prior step (genuine grammar violation of constrained output).

In grammar_bitmask, extend the detect_reasoning_end handling to the non-speculative / bonus-token path (currently the reasoning-end-mid-window logic only runs inside the scheduled_spec_decode_tokens loop; the non-spec branch just fills the bonus mask with should_fill_bitmask()==False). Detect reasoning end for the bonus token too and apply the bitmask to the first post-marker token, so under async scheduling the token right after the marker is constrained rather than free.

Persist reasoning_ended (and reasoning_end_token_index) as soon as the marker is observed during bitmask fill, not only in should_advance during output processing, so should_fill_bitmask on the very next scheduled step already returns True and there is no one-step gap between marker detection and bitmask application.

tests_to_add: Structured-output + reasoning + speculative decoding (MTP) regression: a step window whose generated_token_ids cross the inkling reasoning-end marker (<|content_text|>) with a post-marker draft that is a grammar-invalid special token (e.g. 200028); assert the request completes successfully (post-marker unconstrained tokens rolled back and re-sampled under the bitmask) and is NOT terminated with FINISHED_ERROR.

Async-scheduling (no spec decode) regression for the same reasoning->grammar boundary: assert the first token after the reasoning-end marker is bitmask-constrained and no 500 occurs even if the unconstrained distribution would prefer a special token.

Unit test on the boundary acceptance helper: given advance_token_ids = [valid_json_prefix..., invalid_special_token, ...], accept the valid prefix, roll back the rest, and do not raise / do not mark FINISHED_ERROR when reasoning ended in the same step.

Parser-parity test that InklingParser.is_reasoning_end / is_reasoning_end_streaming fire on <|content_text|>(200004) and <|content_model_end_sampling|>(200006) and NOT on <|end_message|>(200010)/<|message_model|>(200001), guarding the trim boundary against drift.
verification_plan: Statically confirmed: should_fill_bitmask gates on reasoning_ended (__init__.py:361-379); reasoning_ended is set only in should_advance during update_from_output (__init__.py:381-439); grammar_bitmask constrains the first post-marker token only in the spec loop and TOLERATES post-marker rejection (__init__.py:303-331), while scheduler.py:1841 treats accept_tokens==False as FINISHED_ERROR with no tolerance.

Runtime confirmation (not run here, no GPU): serve Inkling-Small-NVFP4 on V1 with a JSON-schema structured-output chat request, once with async scheduling and once with MTP spec decode enabled; capture the generated token stream and confirm an unconstrained special token (e.g. 200028) is emitted immediately after the <|content_text|> marker and reaches accept_tokens. Then apply fix (A)+(B) and confirm the request completes with valid JSON.

Add a targeted engine-core test that injects a synthetic multi-token step [<|content_text|>, 200028] through update_from_output for a structured request with the inkling reasoner and asserts no FINISHED_ERROR after the fix.

evidence.note: Crash site (log points at scheduler.py:1841): should_advance -> trim_reasoning_for_advance -> grammar.accept_tokens; on False sets FINISHED_ERROR/resumable=False and logs 'grammar rejected tokens [...]'. No tolerance for pre-bitmask tokens.

Comment: new_token_ids 'can be a mixed block of reasoning content, then the reasoning end marker, then the start of the grammar content' -- multi-token boundary block under spec/async, exactly the window that leaks.
should_fill_bitmask returns reasoning_ended for reasoner-backed models with enable_in_reasoning False -> bitmask OFF during reasoning; sampling is unconstrained until the marker is seen.

grammar_bitmask detect_reasoning_end: flips apply_bitmask True only AFTER the marker and explicitly tolerates accept_tokens rejection of post-marker drafts ('those drafts predate the bitmask and are not guaranteed valid'). This tolerance is absent in the scheduler output path -- the asymmetry that makes the same situation fatal.

trim_reasoning_for_advance drops tokens up to and including reasoning_end_token_index; it removes inkling's markers but cannot remove a stray unconstrained token (200028) that sits after the marker as 'grammar content'.
XgrammarGrammar.accept_tokens returns False on the first token invalid at the current grammar state; special tokens like <|begin_of_text|> are not valid JSON, so 200028 is rejected.
inkling ships MTP (inkling_mtp) speculative decoding, making the multi-token window / draft path a realistic default trigger for the leak.

Ground truth: 200028=<|begin_of_text|>(special); eos_token_id=200006=<|content_model_end_sampling|>; vocab_size=201024. Confirms 200028 is an in-vocab special token, not the stop token, not out-of-bounds.

follow_ups: Confirm at runtime whether the trigger in the reported incident was async scheduling alone or MTP spec decode (or both); the fix should cover both, but the repro config narrows the minimal test.

Audit every reasoner-backed structured-output model (not just inkling) for the same reasoning->grammar boundary race: any parser whose reasoning-end marker differs from its content-start marker leaves a one-token unconstrained gap under async/spec.

Decide the intended semantics when the model emits a grammar-invalid token at the boundary: silently roll back and re-sample under constraint (proposed) vs. surface a structured-output warning; ensure output-token bookkeeping (num_computed_tokens/placeholders/logprobs) stays consistent with the existing spec-rejection rollback at scheduler.py:1770-1785.
Add a guard/assert that no special token outside the grammar's allowed set can ever be committed as constrained output once reasoning_ended is True, to catch regressions of this class.
